features.title: Measurement questions supply their unit
features.description: When a measurement question has a specified unit, such as BMI in kg/m2, enter the number and the form supplies the unit. You can change or clear the answer.
features.alt: Example BMI question with 40 entered and the unit kg/m2 supplied by the form.
features.caption: Illustrative BMI question; no patient information is shown.

features.title: Read the review question separately
features.description: A knowledge engineer can provide a short question and a quotation from the policy separately from the supporting explanation, making it easier to see what needs your review.

features.title: See what changed after a review request
features.description: A flag can include a summary of the earlier wording and the change made, with links to supporting evidence. You can review the result before marking the flag Fixed or Approved.

features.title: Focus on the review question
features.description: The flag view keeps the question, policy quotation, description and review status in view. Internal classifications and technical identifiers are tucked into Details.
features.alt: Example review flag showing its question, policy quotation and description with Details collapsed.
features.caption: A fictional example of a question for the reviewer.

features.title: Compare Before and After
features.description: Changes shows Before and After beside the flag's description, without repeating the request in another field. If a request has not been implemented, the reason stays visible. Affected questions and evidence links remain available.
features.alt: Example review flag with its description, visible Before and After, and affected question.
features.caption: The request and the resulting change stay together for review.

features.title: Open and close the interactive questionnaire
features.description: The Interactive FHIR Questionnaire button turns blue while its tab is open. Click it again to close the tab, just as you can with FHIR Questionnaire.

features.title: Compare paths in a Decision Table
features.description: Select a node, then click its glowing yellow pin to see its downstream branches stacked in one view. Use Shallower and Deeper to broaden or narrow the comparison. Pinning an outcome shows one branch. Branches without a test case are marked with a coverage error.
features.alt: Two fictional policy paths stacked in Decision Table, with a yellow scope pin and inline questions in the first row.
features.caption: The familiar branch view is repeated for each path. This example uses fictional questions and answers.

features.title: Keep questions beside the path you are reviewing
features.description: The question-results icon cycles through a separate panel, questions inside the branch, and off. The first row opens its question panel automatically. If you move from a row using the panel to a row with questions switched off, the panel follows you. The saved FHIR Questionnaire follows the focused row. Both questionnaires can remain visible beside the tree. Input groups keep your expand or collapse choice.

features.title: See which answers feed each path
features.description: Expand Answers under a question to see its choices grouped by the path they contribute to. Each question has its own groups. The headings use the connector colors and show the next outcome when it is known. Green and red identify the paths.
features.alt: Two treatment checks show different groups of answers under green and red path headings.
features.caption: The same answer can contribute to different paths at different checks. The example is fictional.

features.title: Show uncertainty checks when you need them
features.description: For policies prepared with marked uncertainty checks, the U control inside an outcome node shows or hides the check. A blue border indicates that it is shown. Some checks stay visible when needed for the selected case or a review flag. Showing or hiding changes the view only.
features.alt: A fictional policy tree with uncertainty checks expanded and blue-bordered U controls inside outcome nodes.
features.caption: Use U to inspect the uncertainty check associated with an outcome.

features.title: Open the policy source documents
features.description: Choose Source documents in Medical Validation to list the selected policy's Source and Refined source files. Select a file to open it in its usual editor, including the document viewers supplied in your workspace.

features.title: Keep the tree reachable beside a flag
features.description: While a flag panel is open, pan farther to bring nodes clear of the panel. Opening the panel keeps your current position. Selecting a flag from the flag list can still navigate to its target.

features.title: A reminder about multiple flags
features.description: Already available in 6.4.48, a node can hold several flags. Click its flag icon to choose the flag to read. To add another, right-click the node and choose Add flag on the intended target.

features.title: Find review controls and policy files
features.description: Review actions are grouped together, with status and the legend alongside them. Open Source and Refined source files directly from their named buttons. Show Panel lets you open or close Highlighted Source, and Show Questionnaire groups the questionnaire controls. The legend shows the KE flag badge and the green/red lines used by both ANY OF and ALL OF.
features.alt: Medical Validation toolbar with Status and Legend on the left, grouped review actions and direct policy document buttons on the right.
features.caption: A fictional example of the review controls and source document buttons.

features.title: Keep the tree in view
features.description: Questionnaire panels and Highlighted Source open at compact, matching widths, leaving the remaining space for the tree or Decision Table. These defaults return when you reopen the table or use Shallower and Deeper. Selecting another row keeps your manual width adjustments.

features.title: See shared review progress across rows
features.description: When a branch passes review, its shared steps on the same path also show as passed in other Decision Table rows, including steps before the pin. Different paths keep their own review colors. A failed outcome remains failed even when its earlier shared steps passed.
